# PersonEmailInput

An email address as written to a person record. Reads come back as PersonEmail; the two differ only in required-ness and the server-set dateCreated, since email codes round-trip unchanged.

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `email` * | string (email) | The address. Validated: a malformed value returns 400 INVALID_PARAMETER "'email' is not a valid email address". |
| `type` | string or null | `P` = personal, `W` = work, `O` = other. Defaults to `P`. One of: `P`, `W`, `O`, `None`. |
| `isPreferred` | boolean or null | Whether this becomes the person's preferred address. Documented as defaulting to false; in practice **a newly written address takes the flag**, off whichever address held it before. Writing `true` explicitly **pins** the address: the flag then stops following new additions and survives a merge that brings in a more recently added address. Pinning works on an address the person already holds too — re-writing it with the flag set makes it preferred again. `dateCreated` has only minute resolution, and addresses written within the same minute are not ordered against each other; which of them ends up preferred is not predictable. Space writes at least a minute apart if you need the outcome to be deterministic. |
| `isSubscribed` | boolean or null | Deprecated where Targeted Email is available. `false` is a permanent opt-out — it stores `subscriptionStatus: "U"`, which cannot be reversed. Cannot be sent together with `subscriptionStatus`. |
| `subscriptionStatus` | string or null | `S` = subscribed (the default, and the only status that receives Targeted Email), `N` = neutral, `U` = unsubscribed. `U` is terminal. Only available where Targeted Email is enabled, and not valid alongside `isSubscribed`. One of: `U`, `N`, `S`, `None`. |

`*` = required.
